Anthropic 生命科学负责人 Eric Kauderer-Abrams 在采访中证实了这件事。他的说法是：要做生物学研究，最终的检验标准仍然是真实的实验室工作，光靠计算机模拟不够。一部分实验自己做，一部分和外部合作伙伴做——这和大多数生物技术公司的做法一样。
不过，Anthropic 目前画了一条明确的线：只做临床前研究，不做临床试验，不跟药企抢生意。这也是为了缓解一个现实的信任问题——那些使用 Claude 的大药企（基因泰克、百时美施贵宝、诺和诺德都在列）会担心 Anthropic 从它们的数据中学到什么。

其实我做错的地方在于，没有发现后立刻止损，因为开的少了就没管直接睡觉去了。其实不是这样的，我在桌子上有个纸条，上面写的是，套利之前想清楚，在套谁的利。如果你想不清楚，你就是那个利。永远不要因为金额少而随意。

evidence.quote: NVIDIA、NTU、MIT 团队的 SoL-Pi，就是让 Research Agent 自动发现 Harness 里的 Token 浪费，再通过大规模实验筛掉无效改法。
他们让 Research Agent 观察真实执行轨迹，提出 Harness 改法，再放进大量环境中反复测试。整个搜索覆盖 152 个方向、535 个可执行环境和 3000+ 次实验。

items.summary: cyrilXBT给出Jev适用边界：路由、内容打标等有限选项的高频决策可用其毫秒级判断替代聊天模型，但需要自然语言输出或答案集合不可预先定义的任务仍应交给聊天模型，且仍可能在合法选项中选错。
items.author: cyrilXBT
items.new_information: 按是否需自然语言输出与答案集合是否可定义划界

evidence.quote: jev doesn't generate text. you send it unstructured state plus a set of typed questions, it returns a probability-scored answer to every question at once, in parallel, in 70 to 500 milliseconds. a comparable chat model doing the same class of task runs 3 to 329 seconds, because it's generating tokens sequentially, one at a time, even when the actual output

routing a request before it hits your actual llm call. deciding which of five prompts to use, which tool to invoke, which department a support ticket belongs to. these are typed, bounded decisions, and running them through a full chat completion is paying token generation cost for an answer that was always going to be one of a handful of options.

safety and content tagging at volume. flagging a message as needing review, scoring sentiment, checking a field against a compliance rule, anything you're currently doing with a cheap llm call purely to get a categorical answer back, wrapped in unnecessary natural language you then have to parse out again.

anything requiring the response itself to be natural language. jev never generates a sentence. it can't write your customer's email back to them, it can only decide what kind of email that customer's message needs.

anything genuinely open ended, where the set of possible answers isn't something you can define as a fixed schema in advance. jev needs typed questions with typed possible answers. a task where you don't yet know the shape of a good answer isn't a jev task.

the honest limit worth knowing. bounded, typed output can't hallucinate text, since there's no text. it can still pick the wrong option within a valid schema. this isn't a replacement for verification, it's a replacement for the specific work of deciding, cheaply and fast, which then feeds into whatever actually needs to happen next.

items.summary: SIFT用语言模型作评审对代码改动做成对比较来引导搜索，多数候选不进完整基准；在Polyglot-225上以不足50 CPU小时、150美元将准确率从14%提升至35.1%，TerminalBench 2.1上36.7%对基线29.2%。
items.author: yesnoerror
items.new_information: 以LLM评审替代全量基准的成本与准确率读数

evidence.quote: SIFT (“Self-Improvement via Fast Tree-search”) rewrites the playbook: instead of burning thousands of dollars and days on brute-force benchmarking, it uses a language model as a judge to rapidly compare code changes, guiding search with cheap pairwise votes. Most candidates never touch a full benchmark—only the most promising get the expensive test.

Results: On Polyglot-225, SIFT lifts accuracy from 14% to 35.1% in under 50 CPU-hours and <$150, beating previous bests while using 1/10th the compute. On TerminalBench 2.1, it finds agents scoring 36.7% (vs 29.2% baseline), and generalizes across model families. Judge signals (ρ≈0.68–0.72 with true accuracy) let it move fast without sacrificing quality.
The bottom line: SIFT turns recursive AI self-improvement from a niche for big labs into a practical tool—now you can run a full cycle on a single workstation overnight.

Backpack tokens on Solana:
The SEC does not merely require 1:1 backing or 1:1 redemption.

The infrastructure that is much more directly aligned with what the SEC just described looks more like:
BP is out of scope of SEC's innovation exemption.
Backpack’s stock tokens are not security entitlements. They are tokenized claims on the underlying assets.
They may be redeemable 1:1 for real shares, but that does not mean the tokens themselves carry the same legal rights as the underlying shares.
And Backpack’s tokenized securities were not designed for U.S. investors in the first place.

evidence.quote: First, the reasoning abilities of current AI systems are based non-auto-regressive search (which is what I have always advocated for). But AFAICT, they do it in token space, which is limited and inefficient. I have claimed that human-like reasoning must be a search in continuous representation space. It looks like the industry is moving towards that.

Second, the self-improvement methods, as currently practiced, only work for domains where the quality of outputs can be scored without human intervention, such as mathematics, code, and scenarios that can be simulated accurately. Not anything else. Humans and animals learn new skills way more efficiently than current RL methods.

Third, the multimodal capabilities of current AI assistants generally use separately-trained encoders (that are not LLMs). This is also what I've been advocating. Except that I think the best way to do this is with JEPA trained with self-supervised learning. The research community is clearly moving towards that (3000 papers on JEPA in just 4 years).

Fourth, if LLMs were a path to human-level AI, we would have domestic robots and Level-4 or Level-5 self-driving cars for consumers by now. And we don't. We certainly don't have cars that can learn to drive in 20 hours or practice like any teenager. We're still missing something pretty huge to claim human-level intelligence (let alone superhuman).
I agree with Yann’s observation that LLMs will not lead to human-level AI. But I disagree with his conclusion that JEPA or similar derivatives thereof will.
Human-level intelligence (not AI) requires quantum mechanical substrates operating at ambient temp. Transistors are the show stopper.

LeCun’s point then was that Hinton’s doomerism was “inadvertently helping those who want to put AI research and development under lock and key and protect their business by banning open research, open-source code, and open-access models.”
LeCun’s point today basically is that current SOTA is just software. Good software but much is still lacking.

Secondary pricing shows considerable dispersion too. Meanwhile, Alphabet’s newer 6.5% 2066 bond remains around its issue price.

But CoreWeave’s additional spread over SOFR, issuance discount and tighter protections are evidence of investors demanding more compensation beyond the benchmark rate. The subsequent orderbook also shows demand responding to those concessions.

items.summary: ModularRSI论文把递归自我改进harness的常见缺陷拆为三项：基准污染、单次失败过度归因、整体重写难定位，做法是在2000个独立训练任务上迭代并拆成五个模块分别进化验证，失败即回滚。
items.author: sleepy0x13
items.event: 递归自我改进harness的工程方法
items.new_information: 三类缺陷拆解与五模块分离进化加回滚这一具体做法

evidence.quote: 第一种是 benchmark 污染。很多 self-improving agent 一边拿测试任务改 harness，一边再拿这些任务证明自己变强，最后很难判断到底是 harness 真进化了，还是把题做熟了。ModularRSI 单独做了 2000 个训练任务，harness 在这里迭代，最后冻结下来，再去跑 TerminalBench 2.0 和 SWE-Bench Verified。
第二种是过度相信单次失败。一个 Agent 跑挂了，不代表 harness 一定有问题，也可能只是这次推理走偏。论文的方法是同一道题跑多次，把成功和失败的 trajectory 放在一起看，再跨任务找重复出现的问题。只有某个缺陷反复出现，才值得动 harness。
第三种更像工程问题，不要每发现一个问题，就让 Agent 重写整个 harness。
他们把 harness 拆成 Agent Loop、Tool Use、Observation Management、Context Management、Task Completion Detection 五个模块。哪里出问题就改哪里，每个模块单独进化、验证，最后再合并，还要经过静态检查、diff review 和真实执行测试，失败就回滚。
这三点其实都在回答同一个问题，递归自我改进最难的部分，已经不是让 Agent 有能力修改自己的代码，而是怎么限制它、验证它，以及判断一次修改到底有没有真的让系统变好。

evidence.quote: Following our earlier alert on FomoPeek v1.1–1.2, the SlowMist security team has completed the full technical analysis, based on a joint investigation with the @okx, @OKXWallet_CN security team.

Through static analysis and dynamic verification of historical IPAs obtained from the official App Store, we confirmed that #FomoPeek versions 1.1 and 1.2 contained two malicious modules — apptrace and libapptracecore.
Together, these modules provided capabilities including remote configuration, iOS kernel exploitation, sandbox escape, Keychain decryption, and cross-application data collection.

evidence.quote: 1. jev-ultrafast

给 Claude Code 做上下文压缩。每次工具调用先让 Jev 判断还有没有用，没用的删掉，留下来的原文不重写。
9. jev-review
代码审查前先过一遍 Jev，把高风险改动挑出来，再交给更贵的大模型或人。带本地看板。
15. jev-trader
Monad 测试网上做高频做市。Jev 根据价差和成交方向判断下一步买还是卖，模型延迟大约 81ms。

不直接让 Jev 下单。它判断 toxic flow、市场压力、均值回归之类的状态，再交给原来的策略。
Jev Reviewer, by Ahmad Sofi-Mahmudi, Department of Health Research Methods, Evidence and Impact, McMaster University (MIT licence, runs client-side).

evidence.quote: There’s an old concept called “derived demand” that says most labor is incidental to the outcome you want. That is bad. Essential demand for human labor is tiny. That means most jobs have no moat.

Essential demand for human labor is when the human is part of the product or service. Removing the human fundamentally alters the market offering. Otherwise, the demand for human input is derived; meaning it is secondary, incidental, or merely instrumental to the output.

You probably have no idea who built your house and you likely do not care. That means that all the labor that went into your house is derived demand. The humans who framed and plumbed your house are secondary (or incidental) to the actual economic outcome.

To put that another way; you could remove all human labor inputs from your home and the product remains the same (in terms of value). But if robots and AI built your house, it would probably be cheaper, as human labor accounts for 30% to 50% of the final cost of construction.

Essential Demand Type 3—Liability
Essential Demand Type 4—Affinity

evidence.quote: Got a call from an FBI agent about @vaultaire_app last week.

They told me they found someone using the app. They suspected he used Capture to photograph classified material. When they asked him to open his vault, they believe he may have triggered a duress vault and wiped everything.

Vaultaire was deliberately designed without a master key, backdoor, or recovery mechanism. I have no way to access a user’s vault. I can’t even tell whether he triggered the duress vault. There are no breadcrumbs for me to follow.
I told him I believe in the right to individual privacy. I can’t stop someone from committing a crime. But that shouldn’t require everyone else to give up their privacy.
He asked me to come to the field office to explain more. I told him to call my lawyer. Never heard back.

evidence.quote: Circle Chief Product and Technology Officer Nikhil Chandhok @chandhok  said in a September 16 interview with Bankless @Bankless   that Ethereum is the largest blockchain for USDC. Simply moving existing activity and USDC from Ethereum to Arc would not expand the overall market.

Chandhok believes AI agents will become independent economic actors that need to prove what work they have performed online. He wants Arc to enable agents to record their activities and use cryptographic proofs to verify their work history and actual economic output, creating new on-chain demand.
